skill-upkeep-as-technical-debt.header: Skill upkeep as technical debt: Cunningham's words
skill-upkeep-as-technical-debt.description: "Shipping first time code is like going into debt. A little debt speeds development so long as it is paid back promptly with a rewrite." "Every minute spent on not-quite-right code counts as interest on that debt." [1] He names the failure mode as "the failure to consolidate". The software parallel to skills is an inference, not his claim.

cunningham-wycash.title: Cunningham, The WyCash Portfolio Management System

quick-to-write.title: Quick to write
quick-to-write.script: A skill takes five minutes to write. That is the loan: you get the speed now.

a-running-tab.title: A running tab
a-running-tab.script: Then the statements arrive, one line at a time. The project details changed, a new tool arrived, and a description now overlaps another skill's. None of them is a disaster, and each is a small cost that piles up. Engineers call it technical debt, Ward Cunningham's phrase.

owning-thirty.title: Owning thirty
owning-thirty.script: Writing thirty skills is easy. Owning thirty is the hard part, because the cost was never in writing the skill, it is in keeping it right, month after month.
